title: Find the Number of K-Even Arrays
summary: Given integers n, m, and k, find the count of k-even arrays of size n with elements in [1, m].
statement: Given integers n, m, and k, find the count of k-even arrays of size n with elements in [1, m]. An array is k-even if exactly k indices satisfy a specific evenness condition. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: An adjacent index qualifies exactly when arr[i]*arr[i+1]-arr[i]-arr[i+1] is even.
Count length-n arrays over 1..m with exactly k qualifying indices, modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def count_k_even_arrays(n,m,k):
    modulo=1000000007;even=m//2;odd=m-even
    previous=[[0,0] for _ in range(k+1)];previous[0]=[odd,even]
    for _ in range(1,n):
        current=[[0,0] for _ in range(k+1)]
        for used in range(k+1):
            current[used][0]=(current[used][0]+sum(previous[used])*odd)%modulo
            current[used][1]=(current[used][1]+previous[used][0]*even)%modulo
            if used:current[used][1]=(current[used][1]+previous[used-1][1]*even)%modulo
        previous=current
    return sum(previous[k])%modulo
